summary: Reduce present elements from right to left with JavaScript argument-presence and sparse-array semantics.

target.notes: Pass an explicit argument-presence flag, snapshot length, choose the last present element as the accumulator when initialValue is omitted, then scan downward using HasProperty and invoke callback through JsFunction.Call.

semantics.callback_this: undefined passed through canonical call semantics
semantics.callback_callable_check: TypeError before iteration if callback is not callable

caveats: Explicit undefined is an initial value; omission is not.
Reverse iteration still reads each visited value at visit time, so callback mutations of not-yet-visited indices are observable.

tests.name: uses last present element and scans right to left
holes can make a nonzero-length array effectively empty
future lower index mutation is observed
tests.input: const a=[1,2,3]; const seen=[]; a.reduceRight((acc,v,i)=>{seen.push(v); if(i===1)a[0]=9; return acc+v},0); console.log(seen.join(','));
